audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Jayce/Skill/Jayce/Jayce while the whys[] beside them said the opposite on six rows — 'Jayce's L1 ranged Shock Blast poke chunks Sett' and 'Jayce keeps the L2 edge' sat on Skill rows, while 'Sett stays ahead L4-5', 'Sett's L6 R hard-counters', 'Sett's first item nullifies Jayce's poke' and 'Sett outscales' sat on Jayce rows.
audit.why: The mirror (jayce__sett) settled the chart as Jayce / Jayce / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill. The packet agrees that levels 1-2 are Jayce's and that 3 onward belong to Sett; the mirror is slightly more conservative at level 3 and two items, and I followed it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved to match, phase whys rewritten, and whys[2] and whys[6] de-claimed so neither promises a Sett win on a Skill row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the player to 'commit on Shock Blast's cooldown' seven times without ever giving it, and never priced R's reach.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6s — long enough at rank 1 that walking him down in the gap is a real plan, and short enough late that it stops being one. The Show Stopper is a 400-range cast on 120/100/80s, which is the entire question against a champion whose job is spacing.
audit.corrected: Shock Blast's 16s at rank 1 keyed to the Levels 4-5 phase and the level 3-5 spike; R's 400 range and 120s written into phases[4], spikes[1], spikes[3] and the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) 'Q slow' appears in whys[2], spikes[0], mid and wants.you[1] — Knuckle Down has no slow. (b) spikes[2] says his only escape is 'the E hop in hammer form' — hammer E is Thundering Blow, a knockback; the hop is To the Skies! (Q). (c) Facebreaker is called a grab-stun unconditionally, when a lone target on one side is only slowed.
audit.why: Riot's Sett Q text is empowered attacks plus move speed toward enemies, with no slow. Riot's Jayce E hammer text: 'Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back'; the leap is the hammer Q. Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The mirror recorded the Facebreaker condition and Haymaker's centre-only true damage as the two facts that decide this lane.
audit.corrected: Phantom Q slow removed from all four paths; hammer E and hammer Q correctly separated in spikes[2]; the across-the-minions condition written into phases[2], spikes[0] and mid, with the Haymaker centre cash added to phases[5] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The applicable missing interaction was absent: Jayce's weapon swap is an auto-attack reset, so his burst opens on the swap animation rather than on an ability cast.
audit.why: The swap is 6s and the first attack in cannon form shreds resistances — a player watching for a spell cast has already taken the empowered hit.
audit.corrected: Written into dontsFull[1].d, replacing a line of pure filler.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Jayce on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Shock Blast pokes you from cannon range before you own any answer to it. Take the chip as Grit, hold the wave near you, and wait for Facebreaker.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Jayce and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with Shock Blast.
edits.after: He keeps the edge at 2 — Shock Blast fired through Acceleration Gate gains range and damage. Never stand in the line the gate is drawn on.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Jayce burns Shock Blast.
edits.after: Facebreaker (16s) is online, but it stuns only with a target on each side — pull him across your minions or it is just a slow.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Jayce has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier and his poke is on a real cooldown — Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1. Walk him down inside that window.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Jayce doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: The Show Stopper is online — a 400-range carry that takes a fragile Jayce out of his spacing. Land it and the fight ends before he swaps form.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Jayce. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Jayce. Once his poke stops chunking you, walk him down and cash W with him dead-centre.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Shock Blast and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. It comes down to reach: he swaps to hammer for Thundering Blow's knockback the moment you close.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His weapon swap is an auto reset — the swap is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Sett flips L3 with E Facebreaker and Q slow to force a trade Jayce can't kite.
edits.after: L3 evens out — Facebreaker forces a trade, but only across your minions.

edits.before: Sett outscales a squishy Jayce whose damage falls off against his HP and grit.
edits.after: Late is decided by whether you land the 400-range R on a squishy Jayce first.

edits.before: This is where you flip it: once you have E Facebreaker plus W Haymaker you can Q Knuckle Down onto Jayce, slow him, and force a grit-fueled trade he can't kite. Wait for him to whiff his ranged Q Shock Blast or Acceleration Gate combo, then commit.
edits.after: This is where it evens out: with Facebreaker up, walk in on Knuckle Down's move speed and pull him across your minions so the E stuns instead of slowing. Wait for him to whiff Shock Blast — 16s at rank 1 — and then commit the full trade.

edits.before: R The Show Stopper is a hard counter to Jayce's poke game — flash-R or wall-R him out of position and the fragile mid-range Jayce dies before he retreats to hammer form for the E Thundering Blow knockback.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (120s) hard-counters his poke game — it shuts off To the Skies!, so once the carry starts he cannot hop away, and a fragile Jayce dies before he swaps to hammer for Thundering Blow.

edits.before: With your first item Jayce's poke no longer chunks you meaningfully; walk him down behind minions and all-in — his only escape is the E hop in hammer form, which you outrange with R.
edits.after: With your first item Jayce's poke stops chunking you; walk him down behind minions and all-in — his escape is To the Skies! in hammer form, and Thundering Blow only knocks you back, it does not save him.

edits.before: You stay favoured: Jayce is squishy and your R suppression plus grit sustain means any time you get on top of him he's dead, while his damage falls off against your HP pool.
edits.after: It stays close: Jayce is squishy and dies the moment you land the 400-range carry, but he only has to hold his spacing — his damage does fall off against your HP and Grit.

edits.before: From level 3 on it's your lane — E Facebreaker and Q slow let you stick through his kiting, and the moment he mispositions or whiffs a Shock Blast you Q in and Haymaker him. Track his hammer-form E for the knockback and body-block it.
edits.after: From level 4 it is your lane — Facebreaker across your minions stuns him, and the moment he whiffs a Shock Blast you walk in on Knuckle Down and cash Haymaker dead-centre. Watch his hammer E for the knockback.

edits.before: You stay ahead into items and beyond: R The Show Stopper deletes a squishy Jayce and your grit sustain shrugs off poke, so he can never win the extended fight once you're on him.
edits.after: It stays close into items: The Show Stopper deletes a squishy Jayce the moment it lands, but he only needs to hold his spacing, so the late game turns on whether you reach 400 range.

edits.before: Q slow to stick to him and deny the Acceleration Gate escape
edits.after: Stridebreaker slows to stick through his Acceleration Gate

notes: A real mechanical error was on this page: spikes[2] called Jayce's escape 'the E hop in hammer form'. Hammer E is Thundering Blow, a knockback that pushes YOU away; the hop is To the Skies! (Q). A player waiting out the wrong cooldown before committing loses the all-in. Carried from the mirror and restated here: The Show Stopper shuts off To the Skies!. That comes from the kit file's derived grounding flag, which Riot's own R description does not mention — the mirror published it on Jayce's page, so I matched it rather than leave the two directions saying different things, but it is unverified and the same flag came up in three matchups this slice. One decision worth flagging: at level 3 and at two items the packet is more favourable to Sett than the mirror; I followed the mirror both times.
